title: run-app cache key collides across toolchain builds
commons_coordination: No Commons record filed: MNCS-Commons checkout is on another agent's campaign branch. The owning layer is mncs-language (branch-active).
observed_need: The native-application cache key must bind the exact compiler build (binary identity), so debug and release toolchains never share a cache entry.
current_language_behavior: The cache key binds source, libraries, compiler identity string, inventory, profile, backend, grants, and interface identity. Debug and release builds of the same source report the same nominal identities, so a cache entry written by target/debug/mncs collides with target/release/mncs. Admission then fails closed with 'backend artifact identity does not validate; refusing' instead of recompiling.
why_insufficient: Fail-closed is correct, but the collision turns routine mixed-toolchain use (debug for development, release for environment routing) into a hard failure that requires manual cache deletion. The cache cannot distinguish the two producers.
minimal_reproducer: Run bin/mncs-test-selection once with MNCS=target/debug/mncs, then invoke mncs.test-obligation-selection/1 through mncs-env (which binds target/release/mncs): the second admission fails until native-applications/.mncs is removed.
desired_direction: Fold the compiler binary build identity into the cache key (or namespace the cache root per toolchain), so cross-build reuse becomes a miss, not a refusal.
workaround: Delete the descriptor-local cache (now gitignored) when switching toolchains, or set MNCS_NATIVE_APPLICATION_CACHE_DIR per toolchain.
